subject: math
title: Proportional Reasoning: Unit Rates, Proportions and Proportional Graphs
seo_title: Grade 7 Proportional Reasoning Worksheets (Ontario Math): Free with Answer Key
standard_text: Identify proportional and non-proportional situations and apply proportional reasoning to solve problems
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 proportional reasoning worksheets for the Ontario curriculum: tell proportional from non-proportional tables and graphs, find unit rates, solve proportions like 3/5 = x/20, and solve recipe, speed, best-buy and map-scale problems. 100 math questions with an answer key.
key_big: Proportional means y = kx: y ÷ x is always the same, and the graph is a straight line through (0, 0).
key_sub: Equal ratios come from multiplying, not adding: 3/5 = x/20 gives x = 3 × 4 = 12, not 3 + 15 = 18.
body_html:
What “proportional” means

Two quantities are proportional when one is always the same number times the other: y = kx. The number k is the constant of proportionality. It is also the unit rate, the amount for 1.

Test a table: divide y by x in every column. If you always get the same number, it is proportional.

Proportional graphs

A proportional graph is a straight line through (0, 0). Both parts matter.

Solving a proportion

A proportion says two ratios are equal, like 35 = x20. Three ways to find x:

  • Scale factor: 5 × 4 = 20, so 3 × 4 = 12.
  • Unit rate: 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6, and 0.6 × 20 = 12.
  • Cross products: 5x = 3 × 20 = 60, so x = 12.
Example 1

Solve 35 = x20.

5 × 4 = 20, so multiply the top by 4 as well: 3 × 4.

Answer: x = 12

Example 2: best buy

Yogurt: 650 g for $3.90 or 1 kg for $5.50?

Price per 100 g: $3.90 ÷ 6.5 = 60¢ and $5.50 ÷ 10 = 55¢.

Answer: 1 kg for $5.50

Example 3: speed

A car drives 150 km in 2 h. How far does it go in 5 h?

Unit rate: 150 ÷ 2 = 75 km/h. 5 × 75 = 375.

Answer: 375 km

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
35 = x20 gives x = 18 (add 15 because 20 − 5 = 15)Multiply: 5 × 4 = 20, so 3 × 4 = 12
“y goes up by 2 each time, so it is proportional”Check that y ÷ x is always the same and that (0, 0) fits
A straight line that starts at (0, 2) is proportionalIt must also go through (0, 0)
150 km in 2 h = 300 km/hUnit rate: divide. 150 ÷ 2 = 75 km/h
The bigger package costs more, so it is the worse buyCompare the price for 1 unit (per kg, per 100 g, per bar)

faq.q: What is proportional reasoning in Grade 7 math in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario Grade 7 math curriculum, students tell proportional situations from non-proportional ones and use ratios, unit rates and proportions to solve problems such as recipes, speed, best buys and map scales.

faq.q: How do you tell if a relationship is proportional?
faq.a: In a table, y ÷ x is the same in every column. On a graph, the points lie on a straight line through (0, 0). As an equation, it has the form y = kx.

faq.q: How do you solve a proportion like 3/5 = x/20?
faq.a: Find the scale factor: 5 × 4 = 20, so x = 3 × 4 = 12. You can also cross-multiply: 5x = 3 × 20 = 60, so x = 12.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with proportions?
faq.a: Adding instead of multiplying. For 3/5 = x/20, many students add 15 to get 18, but equal ratios come from multiplying both terms by the same number.

sets.title: Proportional or not? Tables, graphs and situations

items.q: Is y proportional to x?
c: No: the table does not start at 0
items.e: 4 ÷ 1 = 4, 8 ÷ 2 = 4, 12 ÷ 3 = 4, 16 ÷ 4 = 4. The ratio is the same every time, so yes: y = 4x. y − x is 3, 6, 9, 12, so it is not always 3. A table does not need a 0 column.

items.q: Is y proportional to x?
c: No: y ÷ x is not always the same
Yes: y goes up by 2 each time
items.e: 5 ÷ 1 = 5 but 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5, so the ratio changes: not proportional. Going up by the same amount is not enough (that is adding, not multiplying). If you go back one step, x = 0 gives y = 3, not 0.

items.q: Is y proportional to x?
c: No: y ÷ x is not a whole number
No: y goes up by 3 but x goes up by 2
items.e: 3 ÷ 2 = 6 ÷ 4 = 9 ÷ 6 = 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5. Yes: y = 1.5x. The constant does not have to be a whole number. 6 is 2 more than 4, so “1 more” is true only in the first column.

items.q: Is y proportional to x?
c: No: y goes up by 10 each time
items.e: 10 ÷ 1, 20 ÷ 2 and 30 ÷ 3 are all 10, but 45 ÷ 4 = 11.25. Check every column: not proportional. For 4 the value would have to be 40.

items.q: Which table shows a proportional relationship?
items.e: In Table B, 4 ÷ 1 = 8 ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 3 = 4, so Table B. Table A goes up by 2 each time, but 3 ÷ 1 = 3 and 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5. Table D starts like doubling, but 7 is not 2 × 3.

items.q: Which graph shows a proportional relationship?
items.e: A proportional graph is a straight line through (0, 0). Graph B is. Graph C is straight but starts at (0, 2). Graphs A and D start at (0, 0) but bend, so y ÷ x changes.

items.q: Is y proportional to x?
c: No: the line does not pass through (0, 0)
Yes: y goes up by 2 each time
No: the points are not on a straight line
Yes: the points are on a straight line
items.e: When x = 0, y = 2, not 0. So y ÷ x changes (4 ÷ 1 = 4, 6 ÷ 2 = 3): not proportional. A straight line is not enough; it must also go through (0, 0).

items.q: Is y proportional to x?
c: No: y ÷ x is not a whole number
No: the points are not on a straight line
No: the graph must start at (1, 1)
items.e: The points lie on a straight line that starts at (0, 0), so yes. 5 ÷ 2 = 10 ÷ 4 = 15 ÷ 6 = 2.5, and a constant like 2.5 is fine.

items.q: Which situation is proportional?
c: A taxi charges $4 plus $2 per kilometre.
A plant is 5 cm tall and grows 2 cm a week.
A gym charges $50 to join plus $20 a month.
items.e: 0 kg of apples costs $0, and 2 kg costs exactly twice as much as 1 kg: proportional. The other three have a starting amount ($4, $50, 5 cm), so the total for 0 is not 0.

items.q: Which situation is not proportional?
c: A car drives at a steady 90 km/h.
Each bag of milk holds 1.33 L.
Bowling costs $5 for shoes plus $4 per game.
items.e: Bowling 0 games still costs $5 for shoes, and 2 games ($13) is not twice 1 game ($9): not proportional. In the other three, double one amount and the other doubles too.

items.q: Arjun is 12 years old and his sister Leah is 6. Is Arjun’s age proportional to Leah’s age as they grow up?
c: Yes: their ages both go up by 1 each year
Yes: he will always be twice her age
No: the difference stays 6, so the ratio changes
items.e: Now 12:6 = 2:1. In 6 years they are 18 and 12, which is 3:2, not 2:1. The ages keep the same difference (adding), not the same ratio, so they are not proportional.

items.q: Is y proportional to x?
c: No: y goes up by 7, not by 1
Yes: x goes up by 1 each time
items.e: 7 × 0 = 0, 7 × 1 = 7, 7 × 2 = 14, 7 × 3 = 21. Every column fits y = 7x, and (0, 0) is in the table: yes. x going up by 1 says nothing about proportion.

items.q: Is y proportional to x?
c: Yes: y goes up by 2 each time
items.e: A proportional relationship has y = 0 when x = 0. Here y = 3 at the start, so it is not proportional. Going up by 2 each time makes a straight line, but not one through (0, 0).

items.q: Which table is not proportional?
items.e: Table C: 3 ÷ 1 = 3 but 5 ÷ 3 is less than 2. Each y is 2 more than x (adding), so Table C is not proportional. A: y = 3x. B: y = 0.5x. D: y ÷ x is always 53.

items.q: y is proportional to x. What number is missing?
items.e: y ÷ x = 8 ÷ 2 = 4, so y = 4x. When x = 5, y = 4 × 5 = 20. 16 adds 4 again, and 14 adds 2 because x went up by 2: both use adding instead of multiplying.

items.q: y is proportional to x. When x = 6, y = 18. What is y when x = 10?
items.e: y ÷ x = 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so y = 3x. When x = 10: 3 × 10 = 30. 22 adds 4 because x went up by 4. 60 multiplies 6 × 10.

items.q: Which equation shows a proportional relationship?
items.e: A proportional relationship has the form y = kx: y = 4x. With + 1 or + 4, y is not 0 when x = 0.

items.q: A proportional relationship passes through (2, 6). Which point is also on its graph?
items.e: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, so y = 3x. For x = 5: 3 × 5 = 15, so (5, 15). (5, 9) adds 3 to both coordinates, and (6, 2) switches them.

items.q: In which graph is y proportional to x?
items.e: Graph D is a straight line through (0, 0): 3 ÷ 2 = 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5. Graph A is straight but starts at (0, 1). Graph B bends. Graph C goes down and starts at (0, 8).

items.q: Priya earns $15 an hour. Aiden earns $40 a week plus $10 an hour. Whose pay is proportional to the hours worked?
items.e: Priya: 0 hours pays $0, and 2 hours ($30) is twice 1 hour ($15): proportional. Aiden gets $40 even for 0 hours, so his pay is not. The answer is Priya’s only.

sets.title: Unit rates and the constant of proportionality

items.q: 6 cans of juice cost $4.50. What is the cost of 1 can?
items.e: $4.50 ÷ 6 = 450¢ ÷ 6 = 75¢. $27 multiplies, $1.50 divides by 3, and 45¢ divides by 10.

items.q: A car travels 150 km in 2 hours at a steady speed. What is its speed?
items.e: The unit rate is the distance in 1 hour: 150 ÷ 2 = 75 km/h. 300 multiplies instead of dividing, and 148 subtracts.

items.q: 3 kg of apples cost $7.20. What is the price per kilogram?
items.e: $7.20 ÷ 3 = $2.40 per kilogram. Check: 3 × $2.40 = $7.20. $4.20 subtracts 3, and $10.20 adds 3.

items.q: Hana is paid the same amount for every hour. What is her unit rate?
items.e: Pay for 1 hour: $30 ÷ 2 = $15 per hour. Check: $60 ÷ 4 = $15 and $90 ÷ 6 = $15. $30 is the pay for 2 hours, not 1.

items.q: A pump fills 2.4 L in 8 minutes. How many litres does it pump per minute?
items.e: 2.4 ÷ 8 = 0.3 L per minute. Check: 8 × 0.3 = 2.4. 3 L puts the decimal point in the wrong place, and 19.2 L multiplies.

items.q: y is proportional to x. When x = 8, y = 20. What is k in y = kx?
y is proportional to x. What is the constant of proportionality k in y = kx?
items.e: k = y ÷ x = 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75. Check: 0.75 × 8 = 6. 43 divides the wrong way (x ÷ y), and 3 is just the first y value.

items.q: The graph shows a proportional relationship. What is the constant of proportionality?
items.e: Use any point: 7 ÷ 2 = 14 ÷ 4 = 21 ÷ 6 = 3.5. 7 is y at (2, 7), not y for 1. 27 divides x by y.

items.q: The graph shows a proportional relationship. What is the constant of proportionality?
items.e: k = y ÷ x = 2 ÷ 3 = 23. Check: 23 × 9 = 6. 32 is x ÷ y.

items.q: Lucas cycles 9 km in half an hour. What is his speed in kilometres per hour?
items.e: Half an hour is 0.5 h. 9 ÷ 0.5 = 18 km/h: in a full hour he goes twice as far. 4.5 multiplies by 0.5 instead of dividing.

items.q: A Canada goose flies 135 km in 2.5 hours. What is its average speed?
items.e: 135 ÷ 2.5 = 1350 ÷ 25 = 54 km/h. Check: 54 × 2.5 = 108 + 27 = 135. 67.5 divides by 2 and forgets the half hour, and 337.5 multiplies.

items.q: Gas costs $62.40 for 40 L. What is the price per litre?
items.e: $62.40 ÷ 40 = $1.56 per litre. Check: 40 × $1.56 = $62.40. $15.60 is 10 times too big, and $22.40 subtracts 40.

items.q: Sofia runs 100 m in 16 seconds. What is her speed in metres per second?
items.e: 100 ÷ 16 = 6.25 m/s. Check: 16 × 6.25 = 100. 0.16 is 16 ÷ 100, the seconds for 1 metre, not the metres in 1 second. 84 subtracts.

items.q: A 500 g bag of cheese costs $3.25. What is the price per 100 g?
items.e: 500 g = 5 × 100 g. $3.25 ÷ 5 = 65¢ per 100 g. $6.50 is the price per kilogram, and $16.25 multiplies by 5.

items.q: A printer prints 48 pages in 3 minutes. How many seconds does it take to print 1 page?
items.e: 3 minutes = 180 s. 180 ÷ 48 = 3.75 s per page. 16 is the number of pages per minute (the rate the other way round), and 45 subtracts.

items.q: The cost is proportional to the mass. What cost is missing?
items.e: Unit rate: $7 ÷ 2 = $3.50 per kilogram. 3 kg: 3 × $3.50 = $10.50. $8 adds $1 because the mass goes up by 1, and $12.25 is halfway between $7 and $17.50, but 3 is not halfway between 2 and 5.

items.q: Mei walks 12 km in 16 hour. How many kilometres per hour is that?
items.e: 12 ÷ 16 = 12 × 6 = 3 km/h. In 6 sixths of an hour (1 hour) Mei walks 6 × 12 = 3 km. 112 multiplies the fractions, and 13 divides the wrong way.

items.q: A recipe uses 34 cup of sugar for 2 batches of cookies. How much sugar is that per batch?
items.e: 34 ÷ 2 = 38 cup. 32 multiplies by 2, 83 divides the wrong way, and 54 adds 34 + 12.

items.q: Ethan walks 3 km in 45 minutes at a steady pace. What is his speed in kilometres per hour?
items.e: 45 min = 0.75 h. 3 ÷ 0.75 = 4 km/h. Or: 1 km every 15 minutes, so 4 km in 60 minutes. 15 is the minutes per kilometre, not km per hour.

items.q: Which unit rate is the greatest?
items.e: Speeds: 84 ÷ 1.2 = 70 km/h, 150 ÷ 2.5 = 60 km/h, 195 ÷ 3 = 65 km/h, 40 ÷ 0.8 = 50 km/h. 84 km in 1.2 h is the fastest, even though 195 km is the longest distance.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 3:4?
items.e: Multiply both terms by 3: 3 × 3 = 9 and 4 × 3 = 12, so 9:12. 6:7 adds 3 to both terms, and 9:4 multiplies only the first term.

items.q: Which ratio forms a proportion with 2:5?
items.e: 2 × 4 = 8 and 5 × 4 = 20, so 2:5 = 8:20. 5:8 adds 3 and 4:7 adds 2 to both terms. 6:10 multiplies the terms by different numbers.

items.q: Find the missing term: 5:? = 15:24
items.e: 15 ÷ 3 = 5, so divide 24 by 3 too: 8. 14 subtracts 10 from 24 (adding thinking), and 72 multiplies 24 by 3.

items.q: Find the missing term: 7:? = 21:36
items.e: 21 ÷ 3 = 7, so 36 ÷ 3 = 12. 22 subtracts 14 from 36 because 21 − 14 = 7. 108 multiplies by 3 instead of dividing.

items.q: Is 4:6 = 6:9 a proportion?
c: No: you can’t get 6 from 4 by multiplying
items.e: 4:6 = 2:3 (÷ 2) and 6:9 = 2:3 (÷ 3), so yes. Check: 4 × 9 = 36 and 6 × 6 = 36. 4 × 1.5 = 6, so you can multiply. Differences do not matter in a proportion.

items.q: Is 3:5 = 5:7 a proportion?
c: Yes: both ratios are less than 1
No: 7 is not a multiple of 5
Yes: both terms go up by 2
items.e: In a proportion the cross products are equal. 3 × 7 = 21 and 5 × 5 = 25, so no. Adding 2 to both terms changes the ratio: 3:5 = 0.6 but 5:7 is about 0.71.

items.q: Blue and yellow paint are mixed in the same ratio. What number is missing?
items.e: 4:6 = 2:3, so yellow = blue × 1.5. 10 × 1.5 = 15. 13 adds 4 because blue went up by 4, and 12 adds 3 like the last step.

items.q: A pancake recipe keeps eggs and milk in the same ratio. How much milk goes with 7 eggs?
items.e: Unit rate: 250 ÷ 2 = 125 mL per egg. 7 × 125 = 875 mL. 379 adds 4 because the eggs went up by 4, and 1750 multiplies 250 by 7.

items.q: Which proportion is true?
c: 68 = 912
68 = 810
23 = 34
45 = 56
items.e: 68 and 912 both simplify to 34 (cross products: 6 × 12 = 72 and 8 × 9 = 72). The others add 1 or 2 to both terms, which never keeps a ratio the same.

items.q: 5:6 = 15:18 is a proportion. Which statement about it is true?
items.e: In a proportion the cross products are equal: 5 × 18 = 90 and 6 × 15 = 90, so 5 × 18 = 6 × 15. 5 × 15 = 75 and 6 × 18 = 108 are not equal.

items.q: Which ratio is not equivalent to 12:18?
items.e: 12:18 = 2:3. 4:6 and 24:36 also simplify to 2:3. 6:12 subtracts 6 from both terms and equals 1:2, so it is not equivalent.

items.q: Pasta for 4 people uses 300 g. Pasta for 6 people uses 450 g. Is this proportional?
c: Yes: 50 g per person both times
No: 450 is not a multiple of 300
Yes: 75 g per person both times
items.e: 300 ÷ 4 = 75 and 450 ÷ 6 = 75, so the amount per person is the same: yes. In a proportion you compare by dividing, not by subtracting.

items.q: Find the missing term: 1.5:2 = ?:8
items.e: 2 × 4 = 8, so 1.5 × 4 = 6. 7.5 adds 6 to 1.5 because 8 − 2 = 6. 12 multiplies 8 × 1.5.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 2.5:4?
items.e: Multiply both terms by 2: 2.5 × 2 = 5 and 4 × 2 = 8, so 5:8. 4.5:6 adds 2 to both, 4:2.5 switches the order, and 7.5:4 multiplies only the first term.

items.q: Which value of x makes 4:x = 10:25 a proportion?
items.e: 10:25 = 2:5 = 4:10, so x = 10. Cross products: 4 × 25 = 100 = 10 × 10. 19 subtracts 6 from 25, and 62.5 and 1.6 pair the wrong terms.

items.q: Find the missing term: 12:34 = 2:?
items.e: 12 × 4 = 2, so 34 × 4 = 3. 32 multiplies 34 by 2 instead of by 4, and 2.25 adds 1.5 like 12 + 1.5 = 2.

items.q: Which fraction forms a proportion with 615?
items.e: 615 = 25 and 1025 = 25, so they are equal: 1025. 817 adds 2 to both terms, and 1215 doubles only the numerator.

items.q: A trail mix uses nuts, raisins and seeds in the ratio 2:3:1. Which ratio is equivalent?
items.e: Multiply all three terms by 4: 8:12:4. 4:5:3 adds 2 and 3:4:2 adds 1 to each term. 6:9:1 forgets to multiply the seeds.

items.q: Mix A is 3 cups of orange juice and 2 cups of water. Mix B is 4.5 cups of orange juice and 3 cups of water. Do they taste the same?
c: No: Mix B has more juice
Yes: both have 1 more cup of juice than water
items.e: 4.5:3 = 9:6 = 3:2, so the mixes are in the same ratio and taste the same. Mix B has 1.5 more cups of juice than water, not 1 more, but that does not matter.

items.q: Which pair of ratios forms a proportion?
items.e: 1.2 ÷ 3 = 0.4 and 4 ÷ 10 = 0.4, so 1.2:3 and 4:10 are equal. 3.2:5 adds 2 to both terms, 3:1.2 switches the order, and 2.4:3 doubles only the first term.

items.q: Solve: 35 = x20
items.e: 5 × 4 = 20, so multiply the top by 4 too: 3 × 4 = 12. 18 adds 15 to the top because 20 − 5 = 15. Equivalent fractions come from multiplying, not adding.

items.q: Solve: 27 = x28
items.e: 7 × 4 = 28, so x = 2 × 4 = 8. 23 adds 21 because 28 − 7 = 21. 4 is only the scale factor.

items.q: Solve: 49 = 12x
items.e: 4 × 3 = 12, so x = 9 × 3 = 27. 17 adds 8 because 12 − 4 = 8. 3 is the scale factor, not x.

items.q: Solve: 58 = 20x
items.e: 5 × 4 = 20, so x = 8 × 4 = 32. 23 adds 15 to 8. 12.5 and 160 multiply the wrong terms. Cross products check: 5 × 32 = 160 = 8 × 20.

items.q: Solve: x6 = 1518
items.e: 1518 = 56, so x = 5. Or cross-multiply: 18x = 6 × 15 = 90, x = 90 ÷ 18 = 5. 3 subtracts 3 from 6 because 18 − 15 = 3.

items.q: Solve: 7x = 2130
items.e: 21 ÷ 3 = 7, so x = 30 ÷ 3 = 10. 16 subtracts 14 from 30 because 21 − 14 = 7. 90 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: Solve: x15 = 23
items.e: 3 × 5 = 15, so x = 2 × 5 = 10. 14 subtracts 1 from 15 because 3 − 2 = 1. 22.5 multiplies 15 by 32.

items.q: Solve: 6x = 1525
items.e: 1525 = 35, so 6 = 3 × 2 gives x = 5 × 2 = 10. Cross products: 15x = 6 × 25 = 150, x = 10. 16 subtracts 9 from 25 because 15 − 9 = 6.

items.q: Which step solves x8 = 52?
items.e: Multiply both sides by 8: x = 8 × 52 = 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = 20. Check: 208 = 52. 8 + 5 − 2 uses adding, which does not keep fractions equal.

items.q: Solve: 12x = 1620
items.e: 1620 = 45 = 1215, so x = 15. Cross products: 16x = 12 × 20 = 240, x = 15. 16 adds 4 to 12 because 20 − 16 = 4.

items.q: Solve: x12 = 58
items.e: Cross-multiply: 8x = 12 × 5 = 60, so x = 60 ÷ 8 = 7.5. 9 subtracts 3 from 12 because 8 − 5 = 3, and 19.2 is 12 × 8 ÷ 5 (the wrong terms).

items.q: Solve: 34 = 4.5x
items.e: 3 × 1.5 = 4.5, so x = 4 × 1.5 = 6. 5.25 adds 1.5 to 4 (adding thinking). 3.375 multiplies 4.5 × 3 ÷ 4, the wrong way round.

items.q: Solve: 2.4x = 610
items.e: Cross-multiply: 6x = 2.4 × 10 = 24, so x = 24 ÷ 6 = 4. 6.4 adds 4 to 2.4 because 10 − 6 = 4, and 1.44 multiplies 2.4 × 6 ÷ 10.

items.q: Solve: x2.5 = 85
items.e: x = 2.5 × 8 ÷ 5 = 20 ÷ 5 = 4. 5.5 adds 3 to 2.5 because 8 − 5 = 3. 1.6 is only 8 ÷ 5, and 16 divides by 2.5 instead of multiplying.

items.q: Solve: x14 = 3.57
Solve: 0.82 = x15
Solve: x4 = 96
items.e: 96 = 32, so x = 1.5 × 4 = 6. 7 adds 3 to 4 because 9 − 6 = 3. 13.5 is 9 × 6 ÷ 4.

items.q: Solve: 45x = 9100
Solve: 5x = 12.530
items.e: 12.5 ÷ 2.5 = 5, so x = 30 ÷ 2.5 = 12. Cross products: 12.5x = 5 × 30 = 150, x = 12. 22.5 subtracts 7.5 from 30, and 75 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: y is proportional to x. y = 12 when x = 16. What is x when y = 21?
items.e: x ÷ y = 16 ÷ 12 = 43. 21 × 43 = 28. Check: 1216 = 2128. 25 adds 9 to 16 because 21 − 12 = 9, and 15.75 uses the ratio upside down.

sets.title: Word problems: recipes, speed, best buys and maps

items.q: A recipe uses 2 cups of flour for 8 pancakes. How much flour is needed for 20 pancakes?
items.e: 8 pancakes need 2 cups, so 4 pancakes need 1 cup. 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cups. 14 adds 12 because there are 12 more pancakes.

items.q: A recipe uses 2 cups of rice and 3 cups of water. Noah cooks 5 cups of rice. How much water does he need?
items.e: Water = rice × 1.5. 5 × 1.5 = 7.5 cups. 6 cups keeps the water 1 cup more than the rice (adding), but the ratio must stay 2:3.

items.q: Muffins for 12 people use 150 mL of maple syrup. How much syrup is needed for 30 people?
items.e: Unit rate: 150 ÷ 12 = 12.5 mL per person. 30 × 12.5 = 375 mL. 168 adds 18 because there are 18 more people, and 300 just doubles.

items.q: A chili recipe for 6 people uses 450 g of beans. How much is needed for 4 people?
items.e: 450 ÷ 6 = 75 g per person. 4 × 75 = 300 g. 448 subtracts 2 because there are 2 fewer people, and 675 multiplies by 32 instead of 23.

items.q: A car drives at 80 km/h. How far does it go in 3.5 hours?
items.e: Distance = speed × time: 80 × 3.5 = 240 + 40 = 280 km. 240 km forgets the half hour, and 83.5 adds 80 + 3.5.

items.q: A train travels 360 km in 4 hours. At the same speed, how far does it travel in 7 hours?
items.e: Unit rate: 360 ÷ 4 = 90 km/h. 7 × 90 = 630 km. 363 adds 3 because 7 − 4 = 3, and 2520 multiplies 360 × 7.

items.q: Mateo bikes at 18 km/h. How long does it take him to bike 27 km?
items.e: Time = distance ÷ speed: 27 ÷ 18 = 1.5 h = 1 h 30 min. 1 h 50 min reads 1.5 h as 1 h 50 min, but 0.5 h is half of 60 minutes. 9 subtracts 18 from 27.

items.q: Which is the better buy for yogurt?
c: They cost the same per 100 g
items.e: Price per 100 g: $3.90 ÷ 6.5 = 60¢ and $5.50 ÷ 10 = 55¢. 1 kg for $5.50 costs less per 100 g.

items.q: Which is the better buy for granola bars?
c: They cost the same per bar
items.e: Price per bar: $4.20 ÷ 6 = 70¢ and $6.50 ÷ 10 = 65¢. 10 bars for $6.50 is cheaper per bar.

items.q: On a map of Ontario, 1 cm stands for 5 km. Two towns are 7.5 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
items.e: Each centimetre is 5 km: 7.5 × 5 = 37.5 km. 12.5 adds 7.5 + 5, and 1.5 divides by 5.

items.q: On a trail map, 1 cm stands for 2.5 km. A hike is 20 km long. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide by the unit rate: 20 ÷ 2.5 = 8 cm. Check: 8 × 2.5 = 20. 50 cm multiplies 20 × 2.5, and 17.5 subtracts.

items.q: A canoe rental costs $20 plus $10 per hour. Is the cost proportional to the number of hours?
c: Yes: the cost goes up by $10 every hour
No: the price per hour changes
Yes: 2 hours cost twice as much as 1 hour
items.e: 1 hour costs $30 and 2 hours cost $40, which is not twice $30. Renting for 0 hours would still cost $20. So the cost is not proportional, even though it goes up by the same amount each hour.

items.q: It takes about 40 L of maple sap to make 1 L of maple syrup. How much sap is needed for 250 mL of syrup?
items.e: 250 mL = 0.25 L. 40 × 0.25 = 10 L of sap. 160 L divides 40 by 0.25, and 10 000 L multiplies 40 × 250 without changing mL to litres.

items.q: Eggs come in 12 for $4.80 or 18 for $7.02. Which is the better buy?
c: They cost the same per egg
items.e: Price per egg: $4.80 ÷ 12 = 40¢ and $7.02 ÷ 18 = 39¢. 18 for $7.02 costs 1¢ less per egg. Paying more in total does not mean a worse buy.

items.q: At the rink, Nathan skates 1.2 km in 4 minutes. Liam skates 2 km in 7 minutes. Who skates faster?
c: They skate at the same speed
items.e: Nathan: 1.2 ÷ 4 = 0.3 km per minute. Liam: 2 ÷ 7 is less than 0.3 (0.3 × 7 = 2.1 km). So Nathan is faster, even though Liam skates farther.

items.q: On this map, a lake is 6 cm long. How long is the real lake?
items.e: The scale bar shows 2 cm for 15 km. 6 cm = 3 × 2 cm, so the lake is 3 × 15 = 45 km. 19 adds 4 because 6 − 2 = 4, and 90 multiplies 6 × 15 as if 1 cm were 15 km.

items.q: A map has the scale 1:50 000. Two points are 2 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
items.e: 1 cm on the map is 50 000 cm in real life. 2 × 50 000 = 100 000 cm = 1000 m = 1 km. 100 km treats 100 000 cm as metres.

items.q: A hockey player scores 12 goals in the first 20 games. At this rate, how many goals will he score in 65 games?
items.e: Unit rate: 12 ÷ 20 = 0.6 goals per game. 65 × 0.6 = 39. 57 adds 45 because there are 45 more games, and 36 is the goals for 60 games.

items.q: Dog food comes in 3 bag sizes. Which is the best buy?
c: They cost the same per kilogram
items.e: Price per kilogram: $9 ÷ 2 = $4.50, $21 ÷ 5 = $4.20, $35.20 ÷ 8 = $4.40. 5 kg for $21 is the cheapest per kilogram, even though the biggest bag is 8 kg.

items.q: A car uses 6.5 L of gas per 100 km. Gas costs $1.60 per litre. What does the gas cost for a 400 km trip?
items.e: 400 km = 4 × 100 km, so 4 × 6.5 = 26 L. 26 × $1.60 = $41.60. $10.40 is the cost of only 100 km, and $26 gives the litres as dollars.
